content:
Sam: quick proposal — rather than one-size-fits-all tiers, split packaging by workload class: "latency-sensitive", "throughput/batch", and "embedding-heavy". reasoning: different unit economics and SLOs, easier upsell for dedicated lanes. thoughts?

Nina: +1 on segmentation from infra POV. main constraint is routing + kv-cache isolation. can we guarantee latency lanes without huge wasted capacity? :thinking_face:

Ravi: sales note — customers keep asking for "limited bursts" for spikes during cron jobs or batch dedupe. they'd pay for a predictable burst product, but want contract language and visible credits. @Sam can we model a credits add-on?

Leah: finance: need a simple price delta matrix. also need projected ARR uplift and break-even for reserved vs burst capacity. if burst ramps up infra cost a lot we need a hard cap trigger.

Sam: rough sketch for burst clause (for contracts/docs):
```
Burst add-on (optional): grants X burst credits/month.
Burst window: 30s sliding per request
Soft burst: baseline throughput + up to 3x for aggregated 60 minutes/month
Hard cap: no more than 10x baseline per-tenant in any 5 minute window
Overage: beyond credits, charged at 2x list per-token rate
Fallback: if sustained > hard cap, route to cheaper compatible model until contract review
```

Nina: implementation notes: batching + kv-cache means throughput lanes naturally efficient; latency lanes need pre-warmed pools and smaller batch sizes. pre-warm cost implication = reserved capacity component. also quantization profiles differ for embeddings vs chat models.

Sam: OK — proposed product variants:
- Latency Lane (premium): pinned capacity, lower P99, no bursting by default (can add burst credits)
- Throughput Lane (value): autoscaled pools, efficient batching, burst credits supported
- Embedding Lane (metered): optimized kernels, per-embedding pricing, optional reserved pool for low-latency retrieval

Ravi: for GTM, offer a small pilot pack: 100M burst tokens for $X as an add-on. make it consumable via Console purchases and API keys. customers want self-serve top-ups.

Leah: finance asks: simulate three scenarios (low/mid/high adoption) with assumptions: average burst consumption 20% of baseline, uplift 12% ARR for upsell, infra cost multiplier during burst = 1.8. i'll take sims if you share usage profiles.

Nina: question: how do we measure "baseline" per-tenant? rolling 30d median of sustained qps? needs definition in spec.

Sam: good call — propose baseline = 30d median tokens/minute per-tenant, recalculated monthly. include a grace period on onboarding to avoid noisy baselines.

Ravi: legal/GTM ask: need short contract language for pilot and for GA. sample for SLA line: "Burst credits are best-effort; sustained overages may be routed to compatible models per fallback policy." keep it simple.

Leah: we also need a minimal ARR threshold for offering latency lane discounts. suggest $50k/year minimum for dedicated pricing.

ops-bot: created INF-732: implement routing-policy + burst-credit accounting (https://tickets.internal/INF-732)

Sam: launch criteria (draft):
1) Pilot with 2 paying customers (one latency-sensitive, one throughput) for 6 weeks
2) Telemetry: per-tenant token distribution, P95/P99, burst credit consumption dashboards
3) Console UI for purchasing & visualizing burst credits
4) Contract language reviewed by legal + finance sign-off on price matrix
5) Auto-fallback behavior tested end-to-end

Nina: dev-implementation triage: will take ownership of INF-732. ETA: spike + spec by Tue, prototype in 3 sprints.

Ravi: i'll surface pilot customers this week (two warm leads). :thumbsup:

Leah: i'll run the financial sims once I get the usage profiles — target decision meeting next Friday.

Sam: action items: Sam to finalize spec and contract snippet, Nina to spec infra changes (INF-732), Leah to run sims, Ravi to lock pilots. target GA decision after pilot results. thanks all. :raised_hands:
